cases.prompt: Who pays and decides SMP and MA, and what evidence supports an MA claim?
Does not qualifying for SMP automatically produce MA for 39 weeks in every route?
What does the 2023 remedial-order transition say about existing WPA and a cohabiting partner?
Can all retrospective dates be collapsed into one commencement date or used to promise a late claim now?
How does the scheme overview separate its components and the lay DM’s role?
Can the overview be treated as a current list of new-claim benefits or can its US date override the detailed chapter?
What evidence is relevant when an alleged industrial accident has no record or witness?
Does missing an accident-book entry prove no claim can succeed, or does a favourable declaration itself award IIDB?
How do prescribed-disease codes, occupations and rebuttable presumptions fit together?
Does any occupational diagnosis automatically obtain the same presumption and current benefit?
How does IIDB distinguish injury, loss of faculty and disablement assessment?
Can every case be answered using a 14% threshold and 90-day wait?
What separates a regular occupation and earning capacity from all money currently received?
Does missing a REA payment always permanently end entitlement, or is Industrial RA simply the State Pension?
What role does medical opinion play in the source’s US incapacity decision?
Can the limited-capacity provision be a rigid current ESA earnings rule or can the 6/8 April 1987 discrepancy be guessed away?
What happened to the old schemes and pending claims in December 2012?
Do retained compensation/death paragraphs create a new parallel claim route or give damages the same timing effect in every case?

72140   It is not essential that a claimant should be totally incapable of any work. If they are
        capable of some work but because of the relevant loss of faculty he is not likely to
        be able to earn more than the prescribed amount1 they may be treated as incapable
        of work. Earnings includes any remuneration or profit derived from an employment2.

output.excerpt:
72141   This provision is not a rigid “earnings rule” but is a relaxation or modification of the
        usual test of incapacity. It should be applied broadly, looking at the circumstances
        as a whole rather than at one short period in isolation. Thus a claimant's condition
        may be changeable and they may be able to undertake occasional odd jobs or
        seasonal employment earning several pounds a week, but be totally incapable of
        work the rest of the time. The question is whether, taking a long view, they are able,
        in spite of the relevant loss of faculty, to earn more than the prescribed amount.
        Furthermore, entitlement depends solely on whether they are unable because of the
        relevant loss of faculty to earn more than the prescribed amount.
